stories.headline: Banks and Blackstone line up $63B SPV to buy Broadcom AI chips leased to Anthropic

key_facts.fact: On Oct 26, 2026, Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley announced a $63 billion transaction to deploy AI compute capacity built on Broadcom technology for Anthropic, with deliveries expected to start in calendar 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), Blackstone (NYSE: BX), Citi (NYSE: C) and Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) ... today announced a $63 billion transaction to enable the deployment of AI compute capacity, leveraging Broadcom Inc.'s (NASDAQ: AVGO) technology, for Anthropic ... with expected deliveries starting in calendar 2027.

key_facts.fact: A newly formed special purpose vehicle will buy Broadcom XPU AI accelerators and networking gear and lease them to Anthropic; BofA, Citi and Morgan Stanley arrange the first-lien debt and Blackstone is sole provider of the committed second-lien portion.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction will be executed through a newly formed special purpose vehicle ("SPV") ... to support the purchase of Broadcom XPU AI accelerators and networking solutions to be leased to Anthropic. The first lien portion of the financing is being arranged by Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley, with Blackstone as the sole provider of the committed portion of the second lien financing.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom provides residual value support equal to the first-lien portion; its investor deck puts peak exposure at $43 billion, amortizing to zero over five years of lease payments, and says it is not a direct cash outlay.
key_facts.excerpt: Potential liability is any difference between 72.5% of the outstanding amounts owed on the lease and the value of the AI racks received • Peak exposure expected to be $43 billion and decline to zero • RVS is not a direct cash outlay

key_facts.fact: Sources told Reuters the first-lien senior debt is about $43.5 billion, or 69% of the total financing.
key_facts.excerpt: The size of the first lien loans or senior debt is about $43.5 billion, according to two sources familiar with the matter, or 69% of total financing.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom's law firm Sullivan & Cromwell said the financing covers 1.7 gigawatts of AI compute, part of Broadcom's 3.5-gigawatt compute capacity agreement with Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: to enable the deployment of 1.7 gigawatts of AI compute capacity ... This transaction is part of the 3.5 gigawatt compute capacity agreement with Anthropic previously announced by Broadcom.

key_facts.fact: The WSJ reports that CEO Hock Tan spent nearly two months trying to get banks to commit, and closed the deal with 11th-hour concessions over the weekend: higher interest rates and guarantees covering an Anthropic default.
key_facts.excerpt: spooked by rising interest rates and the potential for being overexposed to AI, banks demanded better terms before committing $42 billion. To seal the deal, Tan intervened with 11th-hour concessions, agreeing to higher interest rates and guarantees to cover an Anthropic default.

key_facts.fact: Inside the banks the deal was called 'Project North Star', and some lenders weighed pulling out because they felt underpaid for the risk.
key_facts.excerpt: Some banks grew increasingly anxious about joining 'Project North Star' over the past few weeks ... some felt they weren't being paid enough for the risk and considered pulling out altogether.

stories.headline: Nvidia commits $3B and AMD $1B to Meta's equity raise as Meta adds Vera Rubin capacity

key_facts.fact: Nvidia said it will invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering as part of an expanded partnership on Meta's Muse family of AI models.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA and Meta today announced they will partner to expand their work on Muse and the Muse family of models ... In addition, NVIDIA will invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering.

key_facts.fact: Meta intends to expand its deployment of Nvidia Vera Rubin systems and Vera CPUs, along with Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta intends to expand the deployment of NVIDIA infrastructure, including Vera Rubin and Vera CPUs for next-generation AI agents ... Meta will also deploy NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4

key_facts.fact: AMD said it will invest $1 billion in Meta, bringing the two chipmakers' commitments to $4 billion; AMD said its Helios racks are running at Meta and its EPYC processors power Muse.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia on Tuesday said it would invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering, with AMD announcing it would invest $1 billion. ... AMD said that its Helios racks were running at Meta and its EPYC processors were powering Meta's Muse.

key_facts.fact: On Oct 27 Meta raised the planned size of its equity offerings to $97.5 billion, upsizing the common stock sale to $25 billion from $22.5 billion, priced at $625 a share.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta Platforms on Tuesday raised the planned size of its largest-ever equity offerings to $97.5 billion ... The Facebook parent now plans to raise $25 billion in common stock, compared with $22.5 billion disclosed on Monday. It has priced the shares at $625 each.

key_facts.fact: Reuters notes that the chipmakers' participation adds to concerns about circular capital flows in AI, with suppliers financing one of their biggest customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Their funding interest adds to concerns about an increasingly circular flow of capital in the AI industry, as chip suppliers help finance the expansion of one of their biggest customers.

stories.headline: Intel agrees to buy Israeli quantum-software startup Classiq, reportedly for ~$2.3B

key_facts.fact: On Oct 26, 2026, Intel announced a definitive agreement to acquire Classiq, a Tel Aviv-based quantum computing software provider.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel Corporation today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Classiq, a leading provider of quantum computing software.

key_facts.fact: Intel says combining Classiq's algorithm-synthesis platform with its silicon spin-qubit technology would make it a full-stack quantum provider and add quantum processing units (QPUs) to its CPU, GPU and ASIC portfolio.
key_facts.excerpt: The combination would enable Intel to become a full-stack quantum solutions provider, while also allowing the company to add Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) to its already diverse compute platform portfolio

key_facts.fact: The deal requires regulatory approval and is expected to close in the first half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions and is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

key_facts.fact: Intel did not disclose a price; Bloomberg reported roughly $2.3 billion. Classiq has about 130 employees, has raised over $200 million, and counts BMW and AT&T as customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel's announcement did not include a price. The chipmaker will pay roughly $2.3 billion, according to Bloomberg. ... the startup, which employs roughly 130 people, has brought in over $200 million in funding.

key_facts.fact: Times of Israel says it would be Intel's second-largest acquisition in Israel, after Mobileye, which it bought for over $15 billion in 2017.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal marks Intel's second-largest acquisition in Israel since it bought Mobileye, a Jerusalem-based maker of self-driving technologies, for over $15 billion, in 2017.

key_facts.fact: The deal was announced just ahead of Intel's third-quarter earnings report on Thursday.
key_facts.excerpt: The chipmaker didn't disclose the price it's paying for Classiq, whose clients include BMW AG and AT&T Inc. The [deal] comes just head of Intel's third-quarter earnings report Thursday.

stories.headline: Anduril and Qualcomm unveil BlueChip, a US-assembled Snapdragon laptop for defense and government

key_facts.fact: On Oct 27, 2026, Anduril and Qualcomm unveiled BlueChip, a product line meant to rebuild US computer manufacturing, starting with a laptop designed and assembled in the US and powered by Snapdragon X Series chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, Anduril and Qualcomm Technologies, Inc., are unveiling BlueChip, a new product line dedicated to rebuilding American computer manufacturing. Beginning with a laptop designed and assembled in the United States

key_facts.fact: Anduril has working prototypes and plans to start taking orders in 2027; circuit-board assembly is planned for its Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio.
key_facts.excerpt: Anduril has already developed functional prototypes of the first BlueChip laptop and plans to begin taking orders in 2027. ... with circuit board assembly planned for Anduril's Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio.

key_facts.fact: Components from US and allied-country suppliers account for more than 90% of the prototypes' component procurement cost; the long-term goal is a fully domestic supply chain.
key_facts.excerpt: Components sourced from U.S. and allied-country suppliers account for more than 90% of the BlueChip prototypes' component procurement cost.

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon said the laptop's processors are to be made at TSMC Arizona.
key_facts.excerpt: As for the chips in BlueChip, Qualcomm's Amon told The Verge it intends to manufacture processors for this laptop at TSMC Arizona.

key_facts.fact: Palmer Luckey said some parts, the display among them, are made only in China today, and that the first shipping model will most likely not be 100% American.
key_facts.excerpt: "I think most likely the thing that we ship is not going to be 100-percent American."

key_facts.fact: The first model is a hardened laptop aimed at the military, government, first responders and law enforcement.
key_facts.excerpt: this first product will be a hardened laptop. It will be designed to withstand the most grueling physical environments and meet the security-conscious needs of the military, government, first responders and law enforcement.

stories.headline: Apple puts its 2nm M6 chip in the 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac, pitching faster on-device AI

key_facts.fact: On Oct 27, 2026, Apple announced a 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6, which has a 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple claims up to 30% faster graphics and up to 25% faster AI workloads than M5.
key_facts.excerpt: The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5 ... With additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine

key_facts.fact: The MacBook Pro starts at $1,999 with 16GB of memory (up to 32GB), offers up to 24 hours of battery life, opens for pre-order Oct 28 and ships Nov 6.
key_facts.excerpt: The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starts at $1,999 (U.S.) ... It will begin arriving to customers ... starting Friday, November 6.

key_facts.fact: The Verge says M6 is Apple's first 2nm chip and first shipped in August in the Mac Mini.
key_facts.excerpt: The new M6 processor is Apple's first 2nm chip with a bump to a 12-core CPU, up from 10 cores in the M5

key_facts.fact: Apple also launched an M6 iMac starting at $1,499 and says it is up to 5x faster at on-device AI than the M4 model.
key_facts.excerpt: The 14-inch MacBook Pro starts at $1,999, while the iMac starts at $1,499 ... The new iMac delivers up to 5x faster on-device AI performance than the previous M4 model, Apple said

key_facts.fact: The Verge reports that storage upgrades now cost more because of the memory shortage: +$500 for 2TB and +$1,500 for 4TB.
key_facts.excerpt: increasing that is now more expensive as a result of the current memory shortage. Bumping that to 2TB is an extra $500, while 4TB is now an extra $1,500.

key_facts.fact: The launches come a day before Apple's Oct 28 'Pro and tell' event in Los Angeles, which Bloomberg reports is expected to feature Apple's first touch-screen MacBook Pro.
key_facts.excerpt: The launches come a day before Apple hosts a "Pro and tell" event in Los Angeles on October 28, which Bloomberg News has reported is expected to feature Apple's first touch-screen MacBook Pro

stories.headline: Inference neocloud General Compute raises $100M Series A at $800M valuation

key_facts.fact: General Compute announced a $100 million Series A co-led by Blackbird and Abstract, with Fuse Venture Partners, Village Global and others.
key_facts.excerpt: General Compute, the world's first heterogeneous inference cloud, today announced $100M in Series A funding co-led by Blackbird and Abstract, along with Fuse Venture Partners, Village Global, and others.

key_facts.fact: The startup is valued at $800 million post-money, up from $60 million after its May seed round. A customer deal worth $100 million in annual recurring revenue paved the way for the round.
key_facts.excerpt: A deal with a large customer worth $100 million in annual recurring revenue has paved the way for the company to raise $100 million in Series A funding ... Valued at $60 million after a May seed round, General Compute is now worth $800 million post-money

key_facts.fact: General Compute builds its cloud on inference chips from Nvidia rivals, including a $400 million SambaNova chip purchase deal plus Positron and Cerebras hardware.
key_facts.excerpt: The company struck a $400 million deal to purchase new chips from SambaNova—the first debt financing of inference chips—and now has added Positron and Cerebras to its portfolio of chip suppliers.

key_facts.fact: CEO Finn Puklowski expects to deploy 75 megawatts of compute in 2027. The company rents colocation space and converts former bitcoin-mining sites rather than building data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: Puklowski expects the company to deploy 75 megawatts of computing capacity in 2027, and he suspects he will have access to 200 megawatts of power

key_facts.fact: TechCrunch says the raise comes in a week when CoreWeave hit a 12-month low and Elon Musk predicted '200+ neoclouds' would see 'guppy-level death and consolidation'.
key_facts.excerpt: CoreWeave ... has seen its stock price fall to a 12-month low, and Elon Musk is ... predicting that "200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation."

sources.title: General Compute raises $100 million Series A, countering the neocloud disaster narrative

stories.headline: Imperial spinout Machenta raises $40M, a UK robotics seed record, to teach robots from one demo

key_facts.fact: On Oct 27, 2026, London-based Machenta announced a $40 million seed round co-led by Creandum and Union Square Ventures, which Imperial College London calls the largest seed raise ever by a UK robotics startup.
key_facts.excerpt: Machenta has raised $40 million in the largest ever seed raise by a UK robotics startup. The funding round led by Creandum and Union Square Ventures

key_facts.fact: Machenta is building a robot foundation model that learns new tasks from a single demonstration, pre-trained entirely on simulated data.
key_facts.excerpt: Using a breakthrough AI model developed by Machenta, robots can now learn new tasks from just a single demonstration ... Machenta's model is pre-trained entirely on simulated data.

key_facts.fact: Machenta was founded by Edward Johns, a professor of robot learning at Imperial College London, and his PhD student Vitalis Vosylius, and has a team of around a dozen.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup was co-founded by Edward Johns, a professor of robot learning at Imperial College, London, and his PhD student Vitalis Vosylius ... its team, which numbers around a dozen

key_facts.fact: Machenta declined to disclose its valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: Venture capital firms Creandum and Union Square Ventures co-led the round. Machenta declined to disclose its valuation.

key_facts.fact: It is still a research company with no near-term commercial plans; precise tasks and complex motions remain hard.
key_facts.excerpt: It's a research company and has no plans to go commercial anytime soon. While the model can learn some tasks quickly, more precise tasks and complex motions remain very difficult.
